report_table <- function(x, title, note) {
  gt(x) |>
    tab_header(title = title) |>
    tab_source_note(note) |>
    tab_options(table.font.size = px(13), heading.align = "left",
                column_labels.font.weight = "bold", table.width = gt::pct(100),
                table.background.color = "#19221c", table.font.color = "#e5e9e6",
                heading.background.color = "#19221c",
                column_labels.background.color = "#223329",
                table.border.top.color = "#3b5143", table.border.bottom.color = "#3b5143",
                column_labels.border.bottom.color = "#3b5143",
                table_body.hlines.color = "#303e35")
}

```{r}
#| label: instructor-data-acquisition
#| results: hide
# Use the three download functions from the assignment.
get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr){
    library(tidyverse)
    library(stringr)
    library(httr2)
    library(rvest)
    library(fs)
  
    state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |> str_replace_all("\\s", "")
    
    dir_name <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
    file_name <- fs::path(dir_name, state_formatted)
    
    fs::dir_create(dir_name, recurse=TRUE)
    
    if(!fs::file_exists(file_name)){
        BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"
        RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |> 
          req_url_path("electricity", 
                       "state", 
                       state_formatted) |>
          req_headers(
            `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
            ) |>   
          req_retry(
                max_tries = 4, 
          ) |>
          req_perform(file_name)
    
        resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
    }
    
    TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |> 
        html_element("table") |> 
        html_table() |>
        mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))
    
    if("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)){
        TABLE <- TABLE |> rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
    }
    
    CO2_MWh <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |> 
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    PRIMARY <- TABLE |> 
        filter(Item == "primary energy source") |> 
        pull(Rank)
    
    RATE <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        as.numeric()
    
    GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
        filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
        pull(Value) |>
        str_replace_all(",", "") |>
        as.numeric()
    
    data.frame(CO2_MWh               = CO2_MWh, 
               primary_source        = PRIMARY,
               electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10, # / 100 cents to dollars &
               # * 1000 kWh to MWH 
               generation_MWh        = GENERATION_MWh, 
               state                 = state, 
               abbreviation          = abbr
    )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(state.name, state.abb, get_eia_sep) |> list_rbind()

load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/") |>
      req_url_path("sites",
                   "fta.dot.gov",
                   "files",
                   "2026-09",
                   "2025 Energy Consumption_260806.xlsx") |> 
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_energy.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()

load_ntd_service <- function(){
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  
  # Create 'data/mp02' directory if not already present
  DATA_DIR <- fs::path("data", "mp02")
  fs::dir_create(DATA_DIR, recurse=TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- fs::path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  if(!fs::file_exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query`=paste(
        "SELECT  `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`", 
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000", 
        sep=",")) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete the corrupted file by running `unlink('data/mp02/2025_ntd_service.xlsx')` and try again.")
    }

  read_csv(NTD_SERVICE_FILE) |>
    mutate(flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate))
}

NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
```

```{r}
#| label: preparation-and-analysis
#| results: hide
# Check the columns and summaries after loading the data.
glimpse(EIA_SEP_REPORT)
glimpse(NTD_ENERGY)
glimpse(NTD_SERVICE)
summary(EIA_SEP_REPORT)
summary(NTD_ENERGY)
summary(NTD_SERVICE)

mode_codes <- bind_rows(
  NTD_ENERGY |> distinct(Mode) |> rename(mode = Mode),
  NTD_SERVICE |> distinct(mode)
) |> distinct(mode)
mode_dictionary <- tribble(
  ~mode, ~mode_name,
  "AR", "Alaska Railroad", "CB", "Commuter Bus", "CC", "Cable Car",
  "CR", "Commuter Rail", "DR", "Demand Response", "DT", "Demand Response Taxi",
  "FB", "Ferryboat", "HR", "Heavy Rail", "IP", "Inclined Plane",
  "LR", "Light Rail", "MB", "Bus", "MG", "Monorail/Automated Guideway",
  "PB", "Publico", "RB", "Bus Rapid Transit", "SR", "Streetcar Rail",
  "TB", "Trolleybus", "TR", "Aerial Tramway", "VP", "Vanpool", "YR", "Hybrid Rail"
)
NTD_ENERGY <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(mode = Mode) |>
  left_join(mode_dictionary, by = "mode", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  mutate(Mode = coalesce(mode_name, "Unknown")) |>
  select(-mode_name)
NTD_SERVICE <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  left_join(mode_dictionary, by = "mode", relationship = "many-to-one")
stopifnot(!any(NTD_ENERGY$Mode == "Unknown"), !anyNA(NTD_SERVICE$mode_name))

# Join by agency ID because agency names can be written differently.
NTD_ENERGY <- NTD_ENERGY |> mutate(ntd_id = as.integer(`NTD ID`))
NTD_SERVICE <- NTD_SERVICE |> mutate(ntd_id = as.integer(NTD_ID))
stopifnot(!anyNA(NTD_ENERGY$ntd_id), !anyNA(NTD_SERVICE$ntd_id))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(NTD_ENERGY[c("ntd_id", "mode")]))

# Prepare the answers for the eight questions in Tasks 3a and 3b.
national_grid <- with(EIA_SEP_REPORT, weighted.mean(CO2_MWh, generation_MWh))
ny_grid <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "NY") |> pull(CO2_MWh)
tx_grid <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(abbreviation == "TX") |> pull(CO2_MWh)
source_counts <- EIA_SEP_REPORT |> count(primary_source, name = "states") |>
  arrange(states, primary_source)
rare_sources <- source_counts |> filter(states <= sort(states)[min(3L, n())])
fuel_columns <- names(NTD_ENERGY)[str_detect(names(NTD_ENERGY),
                                           "^Gallons of|^Kilowatt hours|^Kilograms of")]
gallon_columns <- fuel_columns[str_detect(fuel_columns, "^Gallons of") &
                                !str_detect(fuel_columns, "Hydrogen")]
fuel_long <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(fuel_columns), names_to = "fuel", values_to = "quantity") |>
  mutate(unit = case_when(str_detect(fuel, "Kilowatt") ~ "Electricity (kWh)",
                         str_detect(fuel, "Hydrogen") ~ "Hydrogen (source-reported units)",
                         TRUE ~ "Fuel (gallons / gallon equivalents)"),
         fuel_label = str_remove(fuel, "^(Gallons of |Kilowatt hours of |Kilograms of )"))
fuel_summary <- fuel_long |> group_by(fuel, fuel_label, unit) |>
  summarise(quantity = sum(quantity), services = sum(quantity > 0), .groups = "drop")
least_fuels <- fuel_summary |> slice_min(services, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE)
least_used <- fuel_summary |> filter(services > 0) |>
  slice_min(services, n = 1, with_ties = TRUE)
gallon_leaders <- NTD_ENERGY |> group_by(ntd_id) |>
  summarise(agency = first(`Agency Name`), across(all_of(gallon_columns), sum),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(total = rowSums(pick(all_of(gallon_columns)))) |>
  slice_max(total, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE)

# Add up service types so each row is one agency and mode.
# Keep missing service values as NA.
service_modes <- NTD_SERVICE |> group_by(ntd_id, mode) |>
  summarise(agency = first(AGENCY), state = first(state),
            upt = sum(total_upt), pmt = sum(sum_passenger_miles),
            flagged = any(flagged_likely_inaccurate), .groups = "drop")
locations <- NTD_SERVICE |> distinct(ntd_id, state)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(locations$ntd_id),
          !anyDuplicated(EIA_SEP_REPORT$abbreviation))
unmatched_service <- anti_join(service_modes, NTD_ENERGY, by = c("ntd_id", "mode"))
unmatched_energy <- anti_join(NTD_ENERGY, service_modes, by = c("ntd_id", "mode"))
unmatched_ids <- union(unmatched_service$ntd_id, unmatched_energy$ntd_id)

# Use fuel conversion factors for Task 5.
# Natural gas needs a different conversion from diesel.
fuel_factors <- tribble(
  ~pattern, ~kg_co2, ~basis,
  "Bio-Diesel", 10.19, "Diesel proxy for unspecified blends",
  "Bunker", 11.24, "EIA residual fuel oil",
  "Compressed Natural", 52.91 * 0.138, "Natural gas; assumed diesel-equivalent gallon",
  "Diesel Fuel", 10.19, "EIA distillate fuel oil",
  "Ethanol", 0, "Biogenic CO2 excluded",
  "Gasoline", 8.49, "EIA finished motor gasoline",
  "Hydrogen", 0, "No direct carbon emissions; upstream production excluded",
  "Kerosene", 9.88, "EIA kerosene",
  "Liquified Nat|Liquefied Nat", 52.91 * 0.0843, "Natural gas; assumed 0.0843 MMBtu per liquid gallon",
  "Liquified Petroleum|Liquefied Petroleum", 5.75, "EIA propane proxy"
)
fuel_factor_lookup <- tibble(fuel = fuel_columns) |>
  mutate(kg_co2 = map_dbl(fuel, function(name) {
    if (str_detect(name, "Kilowatt")) return(0)
    match <- which(str_detect(name, fuel_factors$pattern))
    stopifnot(length(match) == 1L)
    fuel_factors$kg_co2[match]
  }))
combustion <- fuel_long |>
  left_join(fuel_factor_lookup, by = "fuel", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  group_by(ntd_id, mode) |>
  summarise(combustion_kg = sum(quantity * kg_co2),
            electric_kwh = sum(quantity[str_detect(fuel, "Kilowatt")]),
            non_electric_use = any(quantity[!str_detect(fuel, "Kilowatt")] > 0),
            .groups = "drop")

# Join the three tables and calculate emissions for each agency and mode.
agency_mode <- service_modes |>
  left_join(NTD_ENERGY, by = c("ntd_id", "mode"), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  left_join(EIA_SEP_REPORT |> select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh),
            by = c("state" = "abbreviation"), relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  left_join(combustion, by = c("ntd_id", "mode"), relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(electric_kg = if_else(electric_kwh == 0, 0,
                              electric_kwh / 1000 * CO2_MWh * 0.45359237),
         emissions_kg = combustion_kg + electric_kg,
         kg_upt = emissions_kg / upt, kg_pmt = emissions_kg / pmt,
         complete = replace_na(!flagged & upt > 0 & pmt > 0 &
           emissions_kg > 0 & state %in% state.abb & !ntd_id %in% unmatched_ids, FALSE))

# Add up each agency's totals before calculating emissions per trip and mile.
agency_results <- agency_mode |> group_by(ntd_id) |>
  summarise(agency = first(agency), state = first(state),
            # Count electric passenger-miles before adding up all passenger-miles.
            electric_pmt = sum(if_else(!non_electric_use & electric_kwh > 0, pmt, 0)),
            upt = sum(upt), pmt = sum(pmt), emissions_kg = sum(emissions_kg),
            complete = all(complete),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(kg_upt = emissions_kg / upt, kg_pmt = emissions_kg / pmt,
         electric_share = electric_pmt / pmt,
         size = factor(case_when(upt < 1e6 ~ "Small", upt < 1e7 ~ "Medium",
                                  TRUE ~ "Large"), levels = c("Small", "Medium", "Large")),
         eligible = complete & upt >= 100000 & pmt >= 100000)
eligible <- agency_results |> filter(eligible)
stopifnot(nrow(eligible) > 0L, all(is.finite(eligible$kg_pmt)))
green_winners <- eligible |> arrange(kg_pmt, ntd_id) |> group_by(size) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |> ungroup()
references <- eligible |> group_by(size) |>
  summarise(median_kg_pmt = median(kg_pmt), candidates = n(), .groups = "drop")
electric_winner <- eligible |> arrange(desc(electric_share), desc(pmt), ntd_id) |>
  slice_head(n = 1)
boarding_winner <- eligible |> arrange(kg_upt, ntd_id) |> slice_head(n = 1)
```

## For immediate release

NEW YORK · November 3, 2026 — The Green Transit Alliance announces its 2026 Green Transit Awards. These awards recognize agencies that move passengers with low estimated CO₂ emissions. I used the assignment's transit energy, service, and state electricity data to compare `r fmt(nrow(eligible))` eligible agencies.

**`r paste(green_winners$agency, collapse = "; ")`** win Greenest Transit Agency in their size categories. **`r electric_winner$agency`** wins my original award, Electric Service Leader, for the share of passenger travel on fully electric modes.

I chose two awards, including one of my own, as allowed by the updated instructions. I also answered all eight questions in Tasks 3a and 3b.

### Greenest Transit Agency

This award goes to the agency with the lowest estimated CO₂ per passenger-mile in each size group. This shows how much CO₂ an agency produces to move one passenger one mile. I grouped agencies by annual UPT: small means 100,000 to under 1 million, medium means 1 million to under 10 million, and large means 10 million or more. I chose these groups for the awards; they are not official NTD categories.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-green-awards
green_winners |> left_join(references, by = "size", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  select(size, agency, upt, kg_pmt, median_kg_pmt, candidates) |>
  report_table("Greenest Transit Agency · winners and peer benchmarks",
               "Median is the unweighted median of eligible agencies in the same class.") |>
  cols_label(size = "Class", agency = "Winning agency", upt = "Annual UPT",
             kg_pmt = "kg CO₂ / passenger-mile", median_kg_pmt = "Class median",
             candidates = "Eligible peers") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(upt, candidates), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(kg_pmt, median_kg_pmt), decimals = 3)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-green-awards
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Each winner compared with its size-group median."
#| fig-alt: "Grouped horizontal bars compare each winning agency with its size-class median in kilograms of CO2 per passenger-mile."
award_comparison <- green_winners |>
  left_join(references, by = "size", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  mutate(label = paste0(size, "\n", short_name(agency))) |>
  select(label, Winner = kg_pmt, `Peer median` = median_kg_pmt) |>
  pivot_longer(-label, names_to = "comparison", values_to = "kg")
ggplot(award_comparison, aes(kg, label, fill = comparison)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = 0.7), width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = fmt(kg, 3)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.7),
            hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Winner = green, `Peer median` = "#65776b")) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(title = "Emissions per passenger-mile",
       subtitle = "Greenest Transit Agency winners - lower is better",
       x = "kg CO2 per passenger-mile", y = NULL, fill = NULL)
```

I also compared emissions per UPT. `r boarding_winner$agency` has the lowest value at `r fmt(boarding_winner$kg_upt, 3)` kg CO₂ per UPT. The median eligible agency has `r fmt(median(eligible$kg_upt), 3)` kg. The median is the middle value when agencies are ranked. Shorter trips can lower emissions per UPT, so I used passenger-miles for the Greenest award.

### Electric Service Leader

`r electric_winner$agency` wins Electric Service Leader. Fully electric modes account for `r pct(electric_winner$electric_share)` of its passenger-miles, compared with `r pct(median(eligible$electric_share))` for the median eligible agency. That is `r fmt(electric_winner$electric_pmt)` passenger-miles on fully electric modes.

For this award, I divided passenger-miles on fully electric modes by the agency's total passenger-miles. A mode counts as fully electric only if it reports electricity and no other fuel. I left out mixed-fuel modes from the electric total because the data do not show which passengers used each fuel. If agencies tie, the one with more total passenger-miles wins, followed by the lower NTD ID.

```{r}
#| label: fig-electric-award
#| fig-height: 4.5
#| fig-cap: "The Electric Service Leader compared with the median eligible agency."
#| fig-alt: "Two horizontal bars compare the winner's electric passenger-mile share with the median eligible agency."
electric_comparison <- tibble(
  agency = c("Winner", "Peer median"),
  share = c(electric_winner$electric_share, median(eligible$electric_share))
)
ggplot(electric_comparison, aes(share, agency, fill = agency)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = pct(share)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Winner = green, `Peer median` = "#65776b")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_percent(), limits = c(0, 1.12),
                     breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.25), expand = expansion(mult = 0)) +
  labs(title = "Passenger travel on fully electric modes",
       subtitle = str_wrap(electric_winner$agency, 70),
       x = "Share of passenger-miles", y = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Winner: ", fmt(electric_winner$electric_pmt),
                        " electric passenger-miles.")) +
  guides(fill = "none")
```

Electric service does not always mean low emissions. Producing electricity can release CO₂, and the amount depends on the state's energy mix. That is why I kept electric service and emissions efficiency as separate awards.

## Exploring the data

### State electricity: Task 3a

1. Which five states have the most expensive electricity?

```{r}
#| label: fig-expensive-electricity
#| fig-cap: "Average retail electricity prices by state."
#| fig-alt: "Horizontal bars show the five states with the highest retail electricity prices, in dollars per megawatt-hour."
EIA_SEP_REPORT |> slice_max(electricity_price_MWh, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ggplot(aes(electricity_price_MWh, fct_reorder(state, electricity_price_MWh))) +
  geom_col(fill = green, width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::dollar(electricity_price_MWh, accuracy = 0.1)), hjust = -0.1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_dollar(), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(title = "The five highest retail electricity prices",
       subtitle = "Average state retail price - 1 MWh equals 1,000 kWh",
       x = "Dollars per MWh", y = NULL)
```

These are average state retail prices, not the exact prices transit agencies pay. A higher price does not necessarily mean more CO₂ emissions.

2. Which five states have the dirtiest electricity mix?

```{r}
#| label: tbl-carbon-intensive
EIA_SEP_REPORT |> slice_max(CO2_MWh, n = 5, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  select(state, primary_source, CO2_MWh) |>
  report_table("The five most carbon-intensive electricity mixes", "Higher pounds of CO₂ per MWh means a more carbon-intensive mix.") |>
  cols_label(state = "State", primary_source = "Primary source", CO2_MWh = "lb CO₂ / MWh") |>
  fmt_number(columns = CO2_MWh, decimals = 0)
```

3. What is the average CO₂ emitted per MWh in the U.S.? The weighted average is `r fmt(national_grid)` pounds CO₂ per MWh across the 50 states. I weighted each state by how much electricity it generates. This gives larger electricity producers more weight in the national average.

4. What are the three rarest primary sources, their prices, and their states?

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rarest-sources
EIA_SEP_REPORT |> inner_join(rare_sources, by = "primary_source", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  arrange(states, primary_source, state) |>
  select(primary_source, states, state, electricity_price_MWh) |>
  report_table("The rarest primary electricity sources", "Count = states with that primary source; ties at third place are included. Prices are state retail averages, not the generating cost of the source.") |>
  cols_label(primary_source = "Primary source", states = "State count", state = "State",
             electricity_price_MWh = "Retail $ / MWh") |>
  fmt_currency(columns = electricity_price_MWh, decimals = 2)
```

5. How much cleaner is New York's mix than Texas's? New York emits `r fmt(ny_grid)` lb CO₂/MWh, while Texas emits `r fmt(tx_grid)`. Texas produces `r fmt(tx_grid / ny_grid, 2)` times as much CO₂ per MWh. Put another way, New York's value is `r pct(1 - ny_grid / tx_grid)` lower. This is why I used state-level electricity factors in the emissions calculations.

### Transit fuel use: Task 3b

6. Which five agencies consume the most gallons, and which fuels do they use?

```{r}
#| label: tbl-largest-fuel-users
gallon_leaders |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(gallon_columns), names_to = "fuel", values_to = "gallons") |>
  filter(gallons > 0) |>
  mutate(fuel = str_remove(fuel, "^Gallons of "), share = gallons / total) |>
  arrange(desc(total), desc(gallons)) |>
  select(agency, total, fuel, gallons, share) |>
  report_table("Largest gallon-based fuel consumers · nonzero fuel breakdown", "Electricity and hydrogen excluded from gallon totals. CNG is reported in gallon equivalents; gallon totals do not measure equal energy content.") |>
  cols_label(agency = "Agency", total = "Agency total gallons", fuel = "Fuel",
             gallons = "Fuel gallons", share = "Share of gallons") |>
  fmt_number(columns = c(total, gallons), decimals = 0) |>
  fmt_percent(columns = share, decimals = 1)
```

7. How much of each fuel source does transit use?

```{r}
#| label: fig-fuel-mix
#| fig-cap: "Fuel use by type. Each panel uses different units; the quantities cannot be added together."
#| fig-height: 9
#| fig-alt: "Separate panels show total gallon-based fuels, electricity in kilowatt-hours, and hydrogen in source-reported units. Zero-use categories remain visible through their labels."
ggplot(fuel_summary, aes(quantity, fct_reorder(fuel_label, quantity))) +
  geom_col(fill = green, width = 0.65) +
  geom_text(aes(label = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale())(quantity)),
            hjust = -0.1, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~unit, scales = "free", ncol = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::label_number(scale_cut = scales::cut_short_scale()),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.2))) +
  labs(title = "The energy sources behind U.S. public transit",
       subtitle = "Reported totals - each panel retains its own units",
       x = "Quantity in the panel's units", y = NULL)
```

8. What is the least commonly used fuel source? I counted how many agency–mode pairs reported using each source. `r paste(least_fuels$fuel_label, collapse = ", ")` have the lowest count at `r min(least_fuels$services)`. If I only include sources with some reported use, `r paste(least_used$fuel_label, collapse = ", ")` are least common, appearing in `r min(least_used$services)` pairs. Counting users avoids comparing gallons directly with kWh.

Using more fuel does not automatically make an agency less efficient. It may also serve more passengers or cover longer distances. To compare agencies fairly, I converted their energy use to emissions and divided by the service they provided.

## How I did the analysis

### Loading the data: Tasks 1 and 2

I used the three functions provided in the assignment: `get_eia_sep()`, `load_ntd_energy()`, and `load_ntd_service()`. They download the assigned data and reuse files saved in `data/mp02`. After loading the data, I checked the column types and summaries. I also used `distinct()` to find the mode codes and gave them readable names.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-mode-codes
mode_codes |> left_join(mode_dictionary, by = "mode", relationship = "one-to-one") |>
  arrange(mode) |>
  report_table("Mode codes observed in the assignment data", "Full mode names are shown beside the two-letter codes.") |>
  cols_label(mode = "Code", mode_name = "Mode")
```

### Joining the three tables: Tasks 4 and 5

The provided energy function already groups the data by agency and mode. I added up the service data at the same level, then joined the tables using NTD ID and mode. I joined electricity data using the state abbreviation. Using IDs avoids problems with agency names that are written differently. I also checked for duplicate and unmatched records.

```{r}
#| label: task-four-warmups
# Find UPT in states where nuclear power is the main source.
nuclear_upt <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  semi_join(EIA_SEP_REPORT |> filter(primary_source == "Nuclear"),
            by = c("state" = "abbreviation")) |>
  summarise(upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE)) |> pull(upt)

# Use one metro area per agency so fuel is not counted twice.
metro_lookup <- NTD_SERVICE |> distinct(ntd_id, uza_name)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(metro_lookup$ntd_id))
metro_biodiesel <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  left_join(metro_lookup, by = "ntd_id", relationship = "many-to-one") |>
  filter(!is.na(uza_name)) |> group_by(uza_name) |>
  summarise(gallons = sum(`Gallons of Bio-Diesel`), .groups = "drop") |>
  slice_max(gallons, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE)
```

States where nuclear power is the main source have `r fmt(nuclear_upt)` reported UPT. Among named metro areas, `r metro_biodiesel$uza_name` uses the most biodiesel at `r fmt(metro_biodiesel$gallons)` gallons. I used a semi-join to select the nuclear-power states and a left join to connect agencies to their metro areas.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-data-checks
tibble(
  Check = c("EIA state records", "Energy agency-mode records", "Service agency-mode records",
            "Service agency-modes without energy", "Energy agency-modes without service",
            "Service records flagged by the supplied loader", "Agencies eligible for awards"),
  Count = c(nrow(EIA_SEP_REPORT), nrow(NTD_ENERGY), nrow(service_modes),
            nrow(unmatched_service), nrow(unmatched_energy),
            sum(NTD_SERVICE$flagged_likely_inaccurate), nrow(eligible))
) |> report_table("Data and join checks", "Counts describe separate checks; exclusions may overlap. Missing energy is not converted into zero emissions.") |>
  fmt_number(columns = Count, decimals = 0)
```

### Calculating emissions: Tasks 5 and 6

For each agency and mode, I multiplied fuel use by its CO₂ conversion factor. I calculated electricity emissions with this formula:

$$E_{\mathrm{electric}} = \frac{\mathrm{kWh}}{1000}\times
\mathrm{state\ lb\ CO_2/MWh}\times 0.45359237.$$

Dividing by 1,000 changes kWh to MWh. Multiplying by 0.45359237 changes pounds to kilograms. I included both battery charging and electric propulsion. Then I added each agency's emissions across its modes and divided by its total UPT and passenger-miles. I used the agency totals rather than averaging the individual mode ratios.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-conversion-factors
fuel_factors |>
  mutate(pattern = str_replace_all(pattern, "\\|", " / ")) |>
  report_table("Fuel-to-CO₂ conversions used in Task 5", "Approximate mappings are used where fuel names or units differ. Factors are kg CO₂ per gallon or reported unit.") |>
  cols_label(pattern = "Fuel label", kg_co2 = "kg CO₂ / unit", basis = "Mapping") |>
  fmt_number(columns = kg_co2, decimals = 3)
```

I used the EIA fuel factors requested in the assignment. Some fuels need assumptions. I treated biodiesel like diesel because the provided cleaning code does not keep usable blend details. The factors leave out CO₂ from the plant-based part of ethanol and emissions from producing hydrogen. Natural gas uses the unit assumptions shown in the table. These choices can affect the rankings, so the results are estimates.

### Award rules and limits: Tasks 7 and 8

To avoid giving awards based on very small amounts of service, I required at least 100,000 annual UPT and 100,000 passenger-miles. Agencies also need positive service and emissions for every joined mode, no questionable service flags, no unmatched agency–mode records, and a location in the 50-state sample. The lowest CO₂ per passenger-mile wins within each size group. If efficiency values tie, the lower NTD ID wins.

The provided energy function removes “other fuel” and changes missing fuel values to zero. This means the estimates can miss some emissions. I used each state's average electricity emissions as instructed, even if an agency has a green-energy agreement. The results cover fuel use and electricity generation, not the full impact of building vehicles, construction, or fuel production.

I focused on Greenest Transit Agency and Electric Service Leader. The updated instructions allow two award types, so I did not add the optional Most Emissions Avoided or “worst of” awards.

Overall, these awards highlight two things: moving passengers with low estimated emissions and providing electric service. Looking at both gives a clearer picture than looking at fuel use alone.


```{r}
#| label: final-checks
#| results: hide
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(agency_mode[c("ntd_id", "mode")]),
          all(green_winners$ntd_id %in% eligible$ntd_id),
          all(eligible$electric_share >= 0 & eligible$electric_share <= 1),
          all(eligible$emissions_kg > 0),
          all(is.finite(eligible$kg_upt)))
sessionInfo()
```
